A marketing description states that goods are manufactured, packaged, branded, priced and promoted before being made available to customers. Arrange the following activities in that order:
(1) Price the product
(2) Make the product available to customers
(3) Manufacture the product
(4) Promote the product
(5) Brand the product
(6) Package the product

original_question.stem:
Match List-I with List-II. Each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) Transportation
(B) Decision regarding channels of distribution
(C) Storage or warehousing
(D) Inventory management

List-II
(I) Managing the levels of stock of goods
(II) Storing goods to maintain a smooth flow in the market when production or procurement and sale or use are separated by a time gap
(III) Physically moving goods from one place to another
(IV) Deciding which marketing intermediaries, such as wholesalers or retailers, are to be used

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

items.original_explanation: Transportation is the physical movement of goods, while a channel decision concerns which marketing intermediaries are used. Storage or warehousing supports a smooth market flow when there is a time gap between production or procurement and sale or use; inventory management concerns stock levels. The other mappings interchange these distinct functions.

original_question.stem: A non-profit consumer organisation receives two requests. In case (i), one purchaser asks the organisation to lodge a consumer-court complaint on that purchaser’s behalf about a defective product. In case (ii), a residents’ group asks it to initiate a consumer-court case concerning an unfair seller practice affecting consumers generally; no individual is seeking the case on their behalf. Which pair correctly classifies the organisation’s role in (i) and (ii), respectively?
options: (i) Initiate a case in the general public interest; (ii) lodge a complaint on behalf of an individual consumer
(i) Provide legal assistance; (ii) initiate a case in the general public interest
(i) Lodge a complaint on behalf of an individual consumer; (ii) initiate a case in the general public interest
(i) Encourage consumers to protest; (ii) provide legal assistance

items.original_explanation: A consumer organisation may file a consumer-court complaint on behalf of an individual consumer. Separately, taking the initiative to file a case in a consumer court is identified as a role when the case is in the interest of the general public, not an individual. The two requests therefore match the roles in option C, respectively.

No calculation is required. The two scenarios and their individual-versus-general-interest distinction are supplied in the stem.

You will be able to find some similarities in the features of planning and what you see in real life. Try and identify them. The planning function of the management has certain special features. These features throw light on its nature and scope. (i) Planning focuses on achieving objectives: Organisations are set up with a general purpose in view. Specific goals are set out in the plans along with the activities to be undertaken to achieve the goals. Thus, planning is purposeful. Planning has no meaning unless it contributes to the achievement of predetermined organisational goals. (ii) Planning is a primary function of management: Planning lays down the base for other functions of management. All other managerial functions are performed within the framework of the plans drawn. Thus, planning precedes other functions. This is also referred to as the primacy of planning. The various functions of management are interrelated and equally important. However, planning provides the basis of all other functions. (iii) Planning is pervasive: Planning is requir ed at all levels of management as well as in all departments of the organisation. It is not an exclusive function of top management nor of any particular department. But the scope of planning differs at different levels and among different departments. For example, the top management undertakes planning for the organisation as a whole. Middle management does the departmental planning. At the lowest level, day ‑to‑day operational planning is done by supervisors. (iv) Planning is continuous: Plans are prepar ed for a specific period of time, may be for a month, a quarter, or a year. A firm is establishing a control procedure for one key result area. The manager must set up the procedure and then handle a deviation that qualifies for managerial attention. Arrange the following stages from earliest to latest:
(A) Set the critical point and permissible limit for the key result area.
(B) Identify a deviation that requires managerial attention by assessing it against the permissible limit.
